title: Poles
capsule: The November Uprising (29 November 1830 – 21 October 1831) was a Polish armed insurrection in the Congress Kingdom against Russian imperial rule, launched by military cadets under Piotr Wysocki who stormed Warsaw's Belweder Palace. On 25 January 1831 the Sejm formally dethroned Tsar Nicholas I, mobilizing some 150,000 troops across the Congress Kingdom, Lithuania, and right-bank Ukraine against Russian forces ultimately commanded by Field Marshal Ivan Paskevich. Warsaw fell in September 1831, and the Organic Statute of February 1832 dissolved the Polish constitution and reduced the kingdom to an integral province of the Russian Empire. Tens of thousands of combatants and intellectuals were exiled to Siberia or fled to Western Europe, inaugurating the Great Emigration.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial extent of the November Uprising's control is moderately attested: the insurgency held most of the Congress Kingdom but its precise military frontlines shifted rapidly and are not always precisely mapped in secondary sources.
